passage: Seema stood in the kitchen with her phone in her hand. Yesterday Jomon had promised to come to her cousin's wedding. Today he said, "I never said that. You imagine things. You're too sensitive." She remembered the exact evening, the kettle whistling, his nod. But the certainty was slipping, and that frightened her more than the argument. She opened a note on her phone and wrote the date, the place and what was said. Later she showed it to her friend Nandini, who frowned. "You told me about the wedding promise that same night." Seema breathed out. "So it did happen." Nandini nodded. "Every time he denies something, you end up doubting yourself instead of asking what he did. Maybe talk to the college counsellor." Seema booked a slot for the next morning.

qa.q: What did Jomon promise Seema the day before?
qa.a: He promised to come to her cousin's wedding.

qa.q: What frightened Seema more than the argument?
qa.a: She was frightened that her certainty was slipping and she was starting to doubt her own memory.

qa.q: What could Seema do next, besides the counsellor?
qa.a: She can keep dating her notes, keep checking things with trusted friends like Nandini, and notice whether the denials leave her doubting herself.

qa.q: How does Nandini see Jomon's denials?
qa.a: Nandini sees that each denial makes Seema doubt herself instead of asking what Jomon did, and she wants Seema to get support from a counsellor.

grounding: A partner denies events the protagonist clearly remembers and calls her oversensitive; she writes things down, checks with a friend and seeks counselling.

passage: Pooja was sure Ankita had cancelled their Saturday plans; she remembered the voice note, remembered crying in the auto afterwards. But in their Andheri flat on Sunday, Ankita frowned. 'I never said that. You're so oversensitive, you invent things.' Pooja felt the floor tilt. It was the third time that month. Later, alone on the balcony, she opened her phone notes. The voice note had been deleted, but her own line from Saturday was there: 'A cancelled again, said work.' She called her college friend Farah and read it out. 'That's exactly what you told me that day,' Farah said. 'You're not making things up.' Pooja wrote the date on a fresh page, and before sleeping looked up the counselling centre near her office, saving its number for Monday morning.

qa.q: Who did Pooja call and read the note to?
qa.a: Pooja called her college friend Farah and read it out.

qa.q: What does 'Pooja felt the floor tilt' suggest about her inner state?
qa.a: It suggests Pooja felt shaken and confused, beginning to doubt a memory she had been sure of.

qa.q: What small steps helped Pooja hold on to what really happened?
qa.a: Checking her own written note, reading it to Farah, dating a fresh page and saving a counselling centre's number.

qa.q: How might Ankita want Pooja to see these arguments?
qa.a: Ankita wants Pooja to see her own memories as invented and oversensitive, which lets Ankita avoid owning the cancelled plans.

grounding: Shows a partner denying remembered events and calling Pooja oversensitive, and the wise steps of writing things down, checking with a friend and seeking counselling.

passage:
'Indu, did I tell you on Tuesday that Dev missed my birthday lunch?'
'You did. You sent me a photo of the empty chair. Why?'
'Because now he says it never happened. He says he came, and I'm too sensitive and mix things up.'
'Usha, I was on the phone with you while you sat there.'
'I know. But when he says it so calmly, I start thinking maybe I dreamed it.'
'That's what the calm is for. You end up doubting yourself instead of asking why he skipped it.'
'So what do I do?'
'Write things down when they happen, with dates. Keep the photos. And the counsellor at the student centre is free on Thursdays. I'll walk there with you.'
'You'd come?'
'Of course. And Usha, you're not mixing things up.'
Usha let out a long breath and opened a new note.

qa.q: When is the counsellor at the student centre free?
qa.a: The counsellor is free on Thursdays.

qa.q: How does Usha feel when Dev denies the lunch so calmly?
qa.a: Usha feels unsure and self-doubting, starting to wonder whether the whole day was dreamed.

qa.q: What would you advise Usha to do next?
qa.a: Keep writing events down with dates, keep the photos, and go to the student centre counsellor with Indu on Thursday.

qa.q: Why might Dev want the missed lunch to look like Usha's confusion?
qa.a: If the lunch becomes Usha's mix-up, Dev never has to explain skipping it, so the denial protects Dev.

grounding: Shows a partner denying a missed event and calling Usha too sensitive, while a friend confirms the memory and suggests notes and counselling.
